title: Invertibility of the normalized base coefficient limit comparison
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and $\ell$ a prime. Write $\mathcal R_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq0}(\mathbf Z/\ell^{n+1})_T$, where the factors are discrete constant commutative-ring sheaves on the small pro-etale site of $T$, with reduction transitions [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $d$ be normalized base data and $a$ a base pullback structure of [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-tensor-normalization]. Thus $a.\alpha:h^{-1}\mathcal R_Y\to\mathcal R_X$ satisfies $a.\alpha\,\pi_{X,n}=h^{-1}(\pi_{Y,n})\,\delta_{\mathbf Z/\ell^{n+1}}$, where $\delta$ is the comparison adjoint to preservation of constant sections. Then $a.\alpha$ is an isomorphism. There is no invertibility-on-the-scheme assumption on $\ell$.

source.place: Roots of unity and Integral twist paragraphs.

proof.text: Form the inverse sequence Q of lifted finite rings Z/l^(n+1), with the residue transitions. The successor equations give a natural isomorphism from Q followed by constant sheafification to baseTower. Each Q_n is finite since l is prime.
Use preservation of a countable finite constant-ring tower and transport across this diagram isomorphism.

The normalized constant comparisons form a natural transformation c from the pulled-back base tower to the base tower on X, by naturality with respect to the residue ring homomorphisms; every component is invertible by a.constant_iso.
The composite limit.post followed by limMap c is invertible. Its projections equal a.projection, so joint monicity of the limit projections identifies it with a.alpha.
